Review-only answer to: *if I added this emergency deny and flipped enforce, which observed traffic would it have matched?*

This is not the multi-hop dependency walk in [`docs/blast-radius.md`](https://github.com/zyvorai/zyvor-netra/blob/main/docs/blast-radius.md) and not the CiliumNetworkPolicy review in `insights.PolicyBlastRadius`. There are two complementary paths:

| Path | Evidence | Endpoint / CLI |
|---|---|---|
| Live | Latest non-stale `AgentReport` aggregates (`internal/denysim`) | `POST /api/v1/ebpf/deny/preview` |
| History | Bounded flow deltas (`internal/flowlog` via `internal/counterfactual`) | `POST /api/v1/ebpf/deny/preview-history`, or `deny-preview … --since 1h` |

## Console

**Diagnostics → Deny Preview** posts to the same live and history endpoints, always shows the API caveat, and never applies a rule. Prefer live for DNS/SNI/process when historical name fields are empty.

## Live preview

```bash
netractl ebpf deny-preview cidr 203.0.113.0/24 egress
netractl ebpf deny-preview ip 1.1.1.1 both --protocol UDP --port 53
netractl ebpf deny-preview dns evil.example
netractl ebpf deny-preview sni cdn.example --namespace prod
netractl ebpf deny-preview process curl
netractl ebpf deny-preview port 445 --protocol TCP
```

`POST /api/v1/ebpf/deny/preview`

```json
{
  "kind": "cidr",
  "value": "203.0.113.0/24",
  "direction": "egress",
  "protocol": "TCP",
  "namespace": "prod",
  "limit": 50
}
```

`kind` is one of `ip`, `cidr`, `port`, `dns`, `sni`, `process`. `direction` defaults to `both`. The handler writes nothing to the store, records no audit event, and does not change observe/enforce.

MCP tool: `netra_ebpf_deny_preview` (read-only; available even when `NETRA_MCP_ALLOW_MUTATIONS` is off).

## Historical preview

Uses the controller's flow history (default 7 days / 100000 records; see [`flow-log.md`](https://github.com/zyvorai/zyvor-netra/blob/main/docs/flow-log.md)):

```bash
netractl ebpf deny-preview cidr 203.0.113.0/24 egress --since 1h
netractl ebpf deny-preview port 445 --protocol TCP --since 24h
```

`POST /api/v1/ebpf/deny/preview-history` — same body as live preview, plus optional `since` (duration up to `168h` or RFC3339; default `1h`). `process` is rejected (use live preview). DNS/SNI matches need those fields on retained rows; they are often empty today, so prefer live preview for name-based denies.

MCP tool: `netra_ebpf_deny_preview_history` (read-only).

## Self-lockout check

Both previews return a `lockout` object:

```json
{"risk": "likely", "warnings": [{"protected": "kube-apiserver", "severity": "critical", "reason": "ip 10.96.0.1 overlaps kube-apiserver"}], "checked": ["dns (any resolver)", "kube-apiserver"], "caveat": "..."}
```

`risk` is `none-detected`, `possible` (only a workload-scoped proposal reaches a protected path) or `likely`. The controller compares the proposal with:

- DNS: port 53 and the nameservers in the controller's `/etc/resolv.conf`.
- The kube-apiserver address from `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` / `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT`.
- The controller listen port (`NETRA_LISTEN`).
- Any catch-all prefix (`0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0`).
- `NETRA_PROTECTED_DESTINATIONS`: comma- or space-separated `IP`, `CIDR`, `IP:port`, `[v6]:port`, `:port`, a DNS name (exact or `*.` wildcard) or `process:comm`. A malformed list is ignored and the caveat says so.

This is the controller's own view. It cannot see node-local resolvers, cloud metadata or paths it does not know about, so `none-detected` is not a guarantee, and nothing blocks an apply: enforce stays leased, risk-confirmed and fail-open. List what you cannot lose in `NETRA_PROTECTED_DESTINATIONS`.

## From preview to a leased apply

`netractl denyset plan FILE` runs this preview and the lockout check for every rule of a declarative denyset and returns a plan hash; see [`denyset.md`](https://github.com/zyvorai/zyvor-netra/blob/main/docs/denyset.md). Operators can bound lease creation with [`lease-rails.md`](https://github.com/zyvorai/zyvor-netra/blob/main/docs/lease-rails.md).

## Evidence boundaries

- Live hits are **cumulative counters from the current agent snapshot**.
- History hits are **retained flow deltas** evaluated by `internal/counterfactual` (`FlowLogStore`). Not a column store; first sample after a restart is a baseline only.
- A miss means Netra did not observe (or retain) matching traffic in the window. It does not mean the destination is unused, or that enforce would be a no-op.
- `process` matching (live only) uses sampled `FastPathEvent` rows and `comm` only — not a cryptographic workload identity.
- Stale agents are counted and skipped on the live path.
- Live `truncated: true` means more groups existed than `limit` (default 50, max 200). Totals still include the truncated groups.
- Every response carries a caveat string. Do not render hits as "would be blocked in production" without that sentence.

## Validation

`internal/denysim/denysim_test.go` covers live CIDR matching with stale-agent skip, exact IP + port filters, DNS/SNI name match (case-insensitive), sampled process events, and rejected unknown kinds.

`internal/counterfactual` covers `FlowLogStore` mapping, `PolicyFromEmergencyDeny`, and evaluate-over-history.

No kernel/BPF component — standard `go test ./internal/denysim ./internal/counterfactual ./internal/api` is sufficient.
